status: MD/MM optimization is reopened under A2A. v18 repaired the stale 'mission closed / G1 next' state. v19 lands one correctness fix found during the optimization pass: Hardware::m_ucBatchEnabled now actually mirrors isFirmwareMidiReady(), so UC batch enable/disable transitions can be toggled both ways instead of repeatedly setting only the Microcontroller flag. v21 adds opt-in RT JIT attribution to the MM firmware test and confirms the big steady-state render spikes correlate with synchronous live DSP JIT compilation, not transport clamp/backpressure. v22/v23 add opt-in DSP JIT PC/reason tracing and reject the first naive static graph prewarm attempt. v23 evidence: repeated live JIT PCs are explained by multiple DSP SR-mode chains, not by repeated P-memory invalidation. v24 rejects the next hot-PC existing-chain prewarm prototype by measurement and reverts it. v25 classifies live JIT entries as mostly cold create(), not recreate(). v26 proves a cycle-counted interpreter primitive for future fallback/deferred work, but rejects a naive one-step RT interpreter fallback experiment and reverts that hook. v27 rejects the follow-up queued cold-create fallback prototype: even with a post-callback compile pump and fallback budgets of 128 or 1, the MM firmware test timed out and halted at INVALID PC ff0000; code was reverted and the repo returned to the v26 code state. v28 disables the dsp56k JIT optimizer by default for MD/MM and improved the headless MM spike-amplitude probe, but v30 records Thor's host A/B: MD got worse and MM was neutral. v31 restores optimizer-on as the plugin/default behavior and leaves GEARMULATOR_MDMM_JIT_OPTIMIZER=0 as the diagnostic opt-out path. v32 tests whether the safe UC batch cap can move above 16; evidence rejects it: 20 passes but is slower, 24 fails audio with silence. v33 keeps the mdLib link-ring candidate: it is bit-identical in local smoke/A-B, builds VST3, gives a small Windows/MSVC headless win and a small but host-positive DAW CPU result. v34 ports PR #98 timed DSP1/DSP2 block sync and keeps it after local note-start verification plus Thor host A/B; this is a correctness fix for dropped Monomachine tracks 5/6 note starts, not a perf optimization. v35 keeps PR #98 behavior but replaces the timed-sync edge vector with a fixed 64-entry ring so the realtime scheduler path no longer allocates or front-erases; Thor host A/B accepts keeping the patch. v36 unblocks the MD/MM CI hygiene gates from e1c25ca: mdIdleSelfBranchTest now normalizes Musashi cycle bookkeeping after idle skips, the pmr SysexBuffer test compile errors are fixed, and Windows-only test-harness stack/setvbuf issues are removed so the MSVC MD/MM test set reaches 40/40. Thor host A/B for the v36 VST3 build: MD around 72%, MM around 82%, build behaves well; backgrounded host still adds about +10% CPU, the known old unresolved issue. v38 rejects and reverts the v37 Windows scoped callback-priority candidate: Thor host A/B reported it did not fix the background +CPU usage problem. The backgrounded-host CPU issue remains open; do not reapply the save/boost/restore patch as the fix without new host evidence. v40 rejects and reverts the v39 Windows MMCSS audio-callback priority candidate: Thor host A/B reported it did not fix the background +CPU issue. The issue is now classified as requiring a deeper Windows-host audit of non-audio-thread code paths; do not continue priority-only guesses. v41 builds the promised attribution instrument: a default-off env-gated WinThreadAudit probe (GEARMULATOR_MDMM_THREAD_AUDIT=1) added to jucePluginLib that snapshots all process threads via Toolhelp32, reads GetThreadTimes and GetThreadDescription, and reports per-thread CPU% via OutputDebugStringA for DebugView every 2 s. It starts from the Processor constructor, is a no-op when the env var is unset, and passed local gates: mdAudioIoLayoutTest env-off PASS, VST3 MD+MM build PASS, and headless mmBootFirmwareTest/mdAudioFirmwareTest/mmAudioFirmwareTest all PASS. The deep audit also identified concrete macOS-mindset suspects for the background +CPU: the RmlUI-Renderer GL thread relies on vsync (setSwapInterval 1) which does not throttle hidden/minimized windows on Windows, the pluginLib Controller runs a lifetime 16 ms JUCE timer that flushes every exposed parameter to the UI regardless of visibility, the md Editor runs 16+33 ms dual timers without visibility gating, and enqueueMidiMessages uses startTimer(1). Next acceptance evidence is a Thor host run with GEARMULATOR_MDMM_THREAD_AUDIT=1 comparing foreground vs background per-thread CPU reports. v42 implements Thor's release-purity rule: a release plugin must contain no debug logging, no tracing and no probes. New root CMake option gearmulator_DIAGNOSTICS (default OFF) drives GEARMULATOR_DIAGNOSTIC_LOGGING which now gates every diagnostic path: baseLib LOG macro compiles out, the DSP submodule bridges via DSP56K_DIAGNOSTIC_LOGGING (asmjit trampoline loggers, dspthread MIPS ticker default true->false, jit.cpp/jitblockchain.cpp PC/mode traces), the WinThreadAudit probe is compiled and linked only in diagnostics builds, RealtimeInstrumentation cannot be env-activated in a release build, and mdLib's MDMM_PROFILE/UC_BATCH/JIT_OPTIMIZER/JIT_PC_TRACE env overrides plus mddevice boot stderr messages exist only in diag builds. Measurement protocol is now two builds: clean RELEASE for host A/B, DIAGNOSTICS (temp/cmake_vs26_diag, -Dgearmulator_DIAGNOSTICS=ON) for CPU attribution. Verified: release VST3 strings audit zero probes/markers (MD 23,383,552 B, MM 22,929,408 B; only GEARMULATOR_MM_TIMED_SYNC remains as PR98 functional opt-out), 3/3 firmware gates PASS env-off, diag build reconfigured+proven working (RT/profile output present, PC_TRACE marker in exe).

current_measurements.background_cpu_windows_audit_suspects_v4: Concrete macOS-mindset findings from the v40 deep audit, none patched yet: (1) juceRmlComponent.cpp renderOpenGL uses setSwapInterval(1) for pacing; on Windows a minimized/occluded window's swap does not block, so the RmlUI-Renderer GL thread can spin unthrottled in the background. (2) pluginLib Controller::prepareRealtimeMidiIngress starts a lifetime 16 ms JUCE timer; every tick takes m_controllerServiceLock, processes MIDI and flushes realtime parameter values to the UI regardless of editor visibility. (3) md Editor runs g_presentationTimerId 16 ms + g_panelTimerId 33 ms timers without visibilityChanged gating, polling firmware panel state and pushing RmlUi updates behind hidden editors. (4) Controller::enqueueMidiMessages uses startTimer(1) which on Windows costs a message-thread wakeup per event batch. Acceptance for any fix here is a Thor host foreground/background A/B with the WinThreadAudit probe active.

current_measurements.measurement_methodology_vsthost: Thor discovered a host-measurement confound while recording the 2026-09-30 runs (measurement/MD run.txt, measurement/MM run.txt): loading the plugin into an ALREADY-RUNNING, hours-old VSTHost session produces noticeably higher CPU readings than a FRESH VSTHost start. The MD run was taken in a stale session and showed elevated values; after closing VSTHost completely, the MM run in a fresh session showed good CPU values and the background stuttering improved noticeably (consistent with the earlier report of MD background rise ~+3-5%). RULE for all future host A/B: always start VSTHost fresh for every measurement run, never load test plugins into a long-running session; treat readings from aged sessions as invalid. The saved logs are DebugView-style plugin traces (JIT disassembly, MMU setup, ShellStreams noise), not CPU percentages - the CPU numbers come from the host meter and were reported in chat.
current_measurements.release_purity_v42: Root cause of the MM run2.txt DebugView noise found and compiled out: asmjit AsmJitLogger::_log emitted full x64 disassembly dumps (_log@30 lines, 498 total in that capture) because JitTrampoline::generateExecLoopFunc/ExecUntilCycles/ExecOne attached setLogger(&m_logger) unconditionally, and dspthread.h defaulted m_logToDebug=true so the DSP-thread MIPS ticker logged every ipsStep even in release. active_hypotheses: Pure time-skip for the DSP2 CVR poll loop is unsafe: CVR reads must still invoke m_readCvrCallback so DSP catch-up and host-command acceptance timing remain real.

A full CVR loop accelerator is only viable if it batches taken iterations while still performing CVR reads and checking host-pump/deferred-RX/IRQ/timer/MIDI boundaries between MOVE and BLT. The single-MOVE fast path is rejected by measurement.

DSP2 heavier steady-state wall time is real work, but the large per-block spikes are now attributed to synchronous live DSP JIT compilation inside render callbacks; steady non-JIT windows still hover near the 5.805 ms budget and need separate DSP2 throughput work.

A simple first-PC/static-branch prewarm is insufficient: the trace shows dynamic/low-vector repeated compile events after boot. v23 classified the repeats: P-memory invalidation is not the main cause; the same PCs compile under multiple SR-mode JIT chains. v24 further shows naive hot-PC prewarm across existing chains regresses; a useful fix must avoid creating more wrong/soon-invalidated blocks and must target the actual live create path.

Cycle-counted interpreter fallback is now technically possible, but both attempted cold-create fallback hooks are rejected by evidence: unbounded one-step RT fallback reached INVALID PC ffdf8c, and queued post-callback compilation still reached INVALID PC ff0000 even with fallback budget 1. The issue is deeper than simply compiling queued blocks after the callback; the next attempt must preserve the JIT dispatcher/control-flow contract, not just replace create() with an interpreter step.

Disabling the JIT optimizer reduces synchronous cold compile spike amplitude in the headless MM probe, but Thor's host A/B disproves it as a default plugin policy: MD CPU regresses and MM is neutral. v31 therefore restores optimizer-on default; keep optimizer-off only as a diagnostic opt-out.
